titleStmt.title: Psilocybin produces substantial and sustained decreases in depression and anxiety in patients with life-threatening cancer: A randomized double-blind
titleStmt.author: Roland R. Griffiths
Matthew W. Johnson
Michael A. Carducci
Annie Umbricht
William A. Richards
Brian D. Richards
Mary P Cosimano
Margaret A. Klinedinst

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Psilocybin produces substantial and sustained decreases in depression and anxiety in patients with life-threatening cancer: A randomized double-blind

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: 51 patients with a life-threatening cancer diagnosis and symptoms of depression and/or anxiety, given a high and a very low dose of psilocybin in counterbalanced order
span.quote: The effects of psilocybin were studied in 51 cancer patients with life-threatening diagnoses and symptoms of depression and/or anxiety.

span.label: whether a single high dose of psilocybin, given with psychological support, reduces depression and anxiety in cancer patients, and whether any effect persists
span.quote: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial investigated the effects of a very low (placebo-like) dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) vs. a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg) of psilocybin administered in counterbalanced sequence with 5 weeks between sessions and a 6-month follow-up.

span.label: a randomised double-blind cross-over trial showing large decreases in depressed mood and anxiety sustained at six months, with the mystical-type experience on session day mediating the dose effect
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: existence
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: chronic clinically significant depression and anxiety in patients facing a life-threatening cancer diagnosis
span.quote: Cancer patients often develop a chronic, clinically significant syndrome of psychosocial distress having depressed mood, anxiety, and reduced quality of life as core features, with up to 40% of cancer patients meeting criteria for a mood disorder

span.label: randomised, double-blind, cross-over trial: a very low placebo-like dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) against a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg), counterbalanced, 5 weeks apart, with a 6-month follow-up and community-observer ratings
span.term: randomised, double-blind, cross-over trial: a very low placebo-like dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) against a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg), counterbalanced, 5 weeks apart, with a 6-month follow-up and community-observer ratings
span.quote: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial investigated the effects of a very low (placebo-like) dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) vs. a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg) of psilocybin administered in counterbalanced sequence with 5 weeks between sessions and a 6-month follow-up.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE MYSTICAL-TYPE EXPERIENCE ON SESSION DAY MEDIATES THE DOSE EFFECT: the dose does not reach the therapeutic outcome directly, it reaches it through what the participant experienced during the session
span.quote: Mystical-type psilocybin experience on session day mediated the effect of psilocybin dose on therapeutic outcomes.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PSILOCIN IS A 5-HT2A AGONIST that alters cortical and subcortical activity and brain network dynamics - offered as the pharmacological route and explicitly labelled speculative for the therapeutic effect
span.note: status: The neuropsychopharmacological mechanisms of psilocybin therapeutic effects remain speculative
span.quote: As a 5-HT2A agonist, the psilocybin metabolite psilocin directly and indirectly affects various brain cortical and subcortical areas and alters brain network dynamics

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: TELLING EVERYONE THAT PSILOCYBIN WOULD BE GIVEN EACH SESSION IS WHAT MAKES THE LOW DOSE WORK AS A COMPARATOR: it removes the participant's ability to infer condition from the fact of administration, which is how expectancy was minimised without an inert placebo
span.quote: Instructions to participants and staff minimized expectancy effects.

span.label: 1 mg/70 kg was ASSUMED largely pharmacologically inactive and the authors state that some activity cannot be ruled out entirely
span.quote: Although it was assumed that 1 mg/70 kg would be largely pharmacologically inactive, some pharmacological activity of this dose cannot be ruled out entirely.

span.label: the authors say a far lower dose - around 0.01 mg/70 kg - would have been preferable, to assure inactivity while keeping the instruction that psilocybin would be given each session
span.quote: Thus, it might have been preferable to use an even lower dose of psilocybin (e.g. 0.01 mg/70 kg) to assure pharmacological inactivity while maintaining the benefit of the instruction that psilocybin would be administered on each session.

span.label: the cross-over after 5 weeks precluded a double-blind across-group assessment of high-dose efficacy at that point - the design bought within-subject data at the cost of the between-group comparison
span.quote: Participants were crossed over to the alternative dose condition after 5 weeks. Although this allowed assessment of acute and persisting effects of psilocybin in all study participants, it precluded double-blind assessment of efficacy of the high dose of psilocybin based on across group comparisons after 5 weeks.

span.label: neither the Persisting Effects Questionnaire nor the Community Observer Questionnaire has been independently validated
span.quote: As in previous research, the study documented enduring increases in positive changes in attitudes and mood on both the participant-rated Persisting Effects Questionnaire and on the Community Observer Questionnaire ( Griffiths et al., 2006, 2011). However, neither of these measures has been independently validated.

span.label: clinician ratings were not blinded, and the authors say blinded clinician ratings would strengthen the study
span.quote: Likewise, although the finding of significant decreases in depression and anxiety symptoms on both participant-rated and clinician-rated measures is a strength, the inclusion of blinded clinician ratings would further strengthen the study.

span.label: n = 51, highly educated and predominantly White, which the authors say limits the generality of the conclusions
span.quote: The relatively small sample ( _n_ = 51) that was highly educated and predominately White limits the generality of conclusions.

span.label: the blinding design depends on not disclosing the specific arms, which the authors note may be impossible in settings that require full disclosure
span.quote: Although the low-dose comparison condition and instructions to participants and staff facilitated blinding and minimized expectancy effects, it should be noted that these experimental design features may be difficult to implement in research settings that require complete disclosure of specific study conditions or arms.

span.label: the approach is bounded by extensive exclusion criteria and by the significant time and cost of professional support before, during and after the session
span.quote: the overall approach of treating cancer-related psychological distress with psilocybin is limited by a variety of exclusion criteria (see online Supplementary material) and by the significant time and cost of professional support provided before, during, and after the psilocybin session.

span.label: patients may be reluctant to take part because high doses have sometimes produced transient psychological distress or anxiety
span.quote: Patients may also be reluctant to participate in such an intervention because high doses of psilocybin have sometimes been associated with transient episodes of psychological distress or anxiety in patients

span.label: the neuropsychopharmacological mechanism of the therapeutic effect is stated to remain speculative, and how the enduring effects appear in cortical networks or neuroplastic change remains to be established
span.quote: Precisely how the enduring therapeutically relevant psilocybin effects are reflected in long-term alteration of cortical networks or other neuroplastic changes remains to be established.

span.label: a multisite study in a larger and more diverse population is called for to establish generality and safety
span.quote: A multisite study in a larger and more diverse patient population should be conducted to establish the generality and safety of psilocybin treatment of psychological distress associated with life-threatening cancer.

span.label: BLINDING INTEGRITY WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED. Monitors rated their guess of the dose on a 10 cm line; the high-dose mean was significantly higher, but the distributions overlapped - over 13% of high-dose sessions rated 4 or less and over 12% of low-dose sessions rated 4 or more
span.note: eliminates: monitor expectancy as the determinant of the dose effect - though only partly: the rating distributions overlapped, and the authors claim `some protection` rather than a blind · outcome: partial
span.quote: At the end of each session day, monitors rated their guess of the magnitude of drug dose administered in the capsule that day on a 10 cm line. Although, as expected, the mean (±SE) monitor rating of the dose magnitude of the high psilocybin dose was significantly larger than the low dose (7.0±0.29 vs. 1.7±0.21, _p_ <0.001, planned comparison), the distributions of ratings overlapped, with more than 13% of the high-dose sessions being rated as 4 or less and more than 12% of the low-dose sessions being rated as 4 or more.

span.label: staff understanding of the design was surveyed afterwards: all correctly believed psilocybin was given, and five of eight drew incorrect inferences about the design - three or more dose levels, an inactive placebo, dextromethorphan, or only low doses
span.note: eliminates: staff knowledge of the design as a route for expectancy - five of eight monitors drew incorrect inferences about the study's structure · outcome: held
span.quote: Although all correctly believed that psilocybin had been administered, five of eight made incorrect inferences about the study design or procedures, including possible administration of three or more dose levels of psilocybin across different participants (four monitors), an inactive placebo (one monitor), other psychoactive compounds such as dextromethorphan (one monitor), or only low psilocybin doses (one monitor).

span.label: instructions to participants and staff were designed to minimise expectancy effects, everyone being told psilocybin would be administered at each session
span.note: eliminates: participants inferring their condition from the fact of administration - everyone was told psilocybin would be given at every session · outcome: held
span.quote: Instructions to participants and staff minimized expectancy effects.

span.label: community observers who knew the participant rated behaviour and attitude change independently of the participant and the study staff, and their ratings moved correspondingly
span.note: eliminates: self-report bias as the explanation of the improvement - community observers who knew the participant rated change independently and moved with it · outcome: held
span.quote: Community observer ratings showed corresponding changes.

span.label: adverse events were tracked by dose: no serious adverse events attributed to psilocybin, and no episode met criteria for medical intervention
span.note: eliminates: unreported harm as an alternative reading of the benefit - adverse events were tracked by dose and none met criteria for medical intervention · outcome: held
span.quote: No serious adverse events attributed to psilocybin administration occurred. A number of adverse events occurred during psilocybin sessions, none of which were deemed to be serious.

span.label: the trial was pre-registered - ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00465595
span.note: eliminates: outcome-switching and selective reporting - the trial was registered before it ran · outcome: held
span.quote: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT00465595

span.label: psilocybin
span.quote: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial investigated the effects of a very low (placebo-like) dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) vs. a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg) of psilocybin administered in counterbalanced sequence with 5 weeks between sessions and a 6-month follow-up.

span.label: cross-over
span.quote: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial investigated the effects of a very low (placebo-like) dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) vs. a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg) of psilocybin administered in counterbalanced sequence with 5 weeks between sessions and a 6-month follow-up.

span.label: expectancy effects
span.quote: Instructions to participants and staff minimized expectancy effects.

span.label: death anxiety
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: quality of life
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: depressed mood
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: psilocin
span.quote: As a 5-HT2A agonist, the psilocybin metabolite psilocin directly and indirectly affects various brain cortical and subcortical areas and alters brain network dynamics

span.label: hallucinogen persisting perception disorder
span.quote: There were no cases of hallucinogen persisting perception disorder or prolonged psychosis.

span.label: blinding procedures
span.quote: Overall, we conclude that the blinding procedures provided some protection against a priori monitor expectancy strongly determining outcomes of the psilocybin dose manipulation.

span.label: clinical response
span.quote: The overall rate of clinical response at 6 months on clinician-rated depression and anxiety was 78% and 83%, respectively.

span.label: benzodiazepines
span.quote: Antidepressants and, less frequently, benzodiazepines are used to treat depressed mood and anxiety in cancer patients, although evidence suggesting efficacy is limited and conflicting, and benzodiazepines are generally only recommended for short-term use because of side effects and withdrawal

span.label: psychosocial distress
span.quote: Cancer patients often develop a chronic, clinically significant syndrome of psychosocial distress having depressed mood, anxiety, and reduced quality of life as core features, with up to 40% of cancer patients meeting criteria for a mood disorder

span.label: 5-HT2A agonist
span.quote: As a 5-HT2A agonist, the psilocybin metabolite psilocin directly and indirectly affects various brain cortical and subcortical areas and alters brain network dynamics

span.label: blinding - IN THIS TRIAL A MATTER OF DEGREE THAT THE AUTHORS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Every participant was told psilocybin would be given on each session, so the comparison is high dose against a very low dose, not against an inert placebo. The paper's own verdict is `SOME protection`, not blinding
span.quote: Overall, we conclude that the blinding procedures provided some protection against a priori monitor expectancy strongly determining outcomes of the psilocybin dose manipulation.

span.label: very low dose - A PLACEBO-LIKE DOSE AND NOT A PLACEBO, and the authors say the difference matters: 1 mg/70 kg was assumed largely inactive and they state that some pharmacological activity cannot be ruled out, and that a far lower dose would have been preferable
span.quote: Although it was assumed that 1 mg/70 kg would be largely pharmacologically inactive, some pharmacological activity of this dose cannot be ruled out entirely.

span.label: mystical-type experience - USED HERE AS A MEASURED MEDIATOR ON SESSION DAY, not as a description of how the drug felt. It is the variable through which dose reaches therapeutic outcome, which makes it part of the causal claim rather than a side observation
span.quote: Mystical-type psilocybin experience on session day mediated the effect of psilocybin dose on therapeutic outcomes.

span.label: critiques → antidepressants and benzodiazepines for depressed mood and anxiety in cancer patients, where the efficacy evidence is called limited and conflicting and benzodiazepines are recommended only short-term
span.quote: Antidepressants and, less frequently, benzodiazepines are used to treat depressed mood and anxiety in cancer patients, although evidence suggesting efficacy is limited and conflicting, and benzodiazepines are generally only recommended for short-term use because of side effects and withdrawal

span.label: critiques → psychological approaches to emotional distress in cancer, which have shown only small to medium effects with low quality of reporting in many trials
span.quote: Although psychological approaches have shown only small to medium effects in treating emotional distress and quality of life, with low quality of reporting in many trials

span.label: replicates → the authors' own previous psilocybin work in healthy volunteers, whose adverse-effect and persisting-effect patterns this trial reproduces in patients
span.quote: As in previous research, the study documented enduring increases in positive changes in attitudes and mood on both the participant-rated Persisting Effects Questionnaire and on the Community Observer Questionnaire ( Griffiths et al., 2006, 2011). However, neither of these measures has been independently validated.

span.label: psilocybin —causes→ depressed mood
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: psilocybin —causes→ death anxiety
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: psilocybin —causes→ quality of life
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: psilocin —is-a→ 5-HT2A agonist
span.quote: As a 5-HT2A agonist, the psilocybin metabolite psilocin directly and indirectly affects various brain cortical and subcortical areas and alters brain network dynamics

span.label: high-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated depressed mood and anxiety, with increases in quality of life, life meaning and optimism and decreases in death anxiety
span.quote: High-dose psilocybin produced large decreases in clinician- and self-rated measures of depressed mood and anxiety, along with increases in quality of life, life meaning, and optimism, and decreases in death anxiety.

span.label: the changes were sustained at 6-month follow-up, with about 80% of participants still showing clinically significant decreases
span.quote: At 6-month follow-up, these changes were sustained, with about 80% of participants continuing to show clinically significant decreases in depressed mood and anxiety.

span.label: the mystical-type experience on session day mediated the effect of dose on therapeutic outcome
span.quote: Mystical-type psilocybin experience on session day mediated the effect of psilocybin dose on therapeutic outcomes.

span.label: no serious adverse events were attributed to psilocybin and no episode met criteria for medical intervention; there were no cases of hallucinogen persisting perception disorder or prolonged psychosis
span.quote: There were no cases of hallucinogen persisting perception disorder or prolonged psychosis.

span.label: clinical response at 6 months on clinician-rated depression 78% and anxiety 83% — None
span.quote: The overall rate of clinical response at 6 months on clinician-rated depression and anxiety was 78% and 83%, respectively.

span.label: 51 cancer patients with life-threatening diagnoses — None
span.quote: The effects of psilocybin were studied in 51 cancer patients with life-threatening diagnoses and symptoms of depression and/or anxiety.

span.label: elevated systolic blood pressure in 34% of high-dose and 17% of low-dose sessions — None
span.quote: an episode of elevated systolic blood pressure (>160 mm Hg at one or more time-point) occurred in 34% of participants in the high-dose session and 17% of participants in the low-dose session.

span.label: psychological discomfort in 32% of high-dose and 12% of low-dose sessions; anxiety in 26% and 15% — None
span.quote: Psychological discomfort (any type) occurred in 32% of participants in the high-dose session and 12% in the low-dose session. An episode of anxiety occurred in 26% of participants in the high-dose session and 15% in the low-dose session. One participant had a transient episode of paranoid ideation

span.label: up to 40% of cancer patients meet criteria for a mood disorder — None
span.quote: Cancer patients often develop a chronic, clinically significant syndrome of psychosocial distress having depressed mood, anxiety, and reduced quality of life as core features, with up to 40% of cancer patients meeting criteria for a mood disorder

span.label: monitor dose-magnitude ratings 7.0±0.29 for the high dose against 1.7±0.21 for the low dose, p<0.001 by planned comparison, with overlapping distributions
span.quote: At the end of each session day, monitors rated their guess of the magnitude of drug dose administered in the capsule that day on a 10 cm line. Although, as expected, the mean (±SE) monitor rating of the dose magnitude of the high psilocybin dose was significantly larger than the low dose (7.0±0.29 vs. 1.7±0.21, _p_ <0.001, planned comparison), the distributions of ratings overlapped, with more than 13% of the high-dose sessions being rated as 4 or less and more than 12% of the low-dose sessions being rated as 4 or more.

span.quote: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial investigated the effects of a very low (placebo-like) dose (1 or 3 mg/70 kg) vs. a high dose (22 or 30 mg/70 kg) of psilocybin administered in counterbalanced sequence with 5 weeks between sessions and a 6-month follow-up.

span.label: monitor-rated guess of the dose magnitude, used to test the blind
span.term: monitor-rated guess of the dose magnitude, used to test the blind
span.quote: At the end of each session day, monitors rated their guess of the magnitude of drug dose administered in the capsule that day on a 10 cm line. Although, as expected, the mean (±SE) monitor rating of the dose magnitude of the high psilocybin dose was significantly larger than the low dose (7.0±0.29 vs. 1.7±0.21, _p_ <0.001, planned comparison), the distributions of ratings overlapped, with more than 13% of the high-dose sessions being rated as 4 or less and more than 12% of the low-dose sessions being rated as 4 or more.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1177/0269881116675513.
